PyTorch’s [DataLoader documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html) confirms iterator creation can consume RNG state; its generator controls sampling and worker seeds. Recommended design: separate diagnostic dataset, sampler, workers, negative sampler, and dedicated generators; never iterate the training loader or share mutable sampling state. Seed Python/NumPy in diagnostic workers, preferably precompute diagnostic sequences and negatives. Around diagnostics, save/restore Python, NumPy, Torch CPU/CUDA and explicit-generator states in `try/finally`; restore model training modes and avoid buffer updates. [fork_rng](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/random.html) handles Torch RNG only; parent-state restoration cannot rewind training workers or prefetched batches. Verify identical subsequent training batches, negatives, and updates with diagnostics enabled versus disabled.

Proposed aggregation: hold users, targets, candidates, perturbation draws, and masking rules fixed across checkpoints. Compute each user’s paired effect, perturbed minus original; average repeated perturbations within user, then users within dataset, then equally across Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Report signed effects, per-dataset results, and user-cluster bootstrap intervals, resampling each user’s complete checkpoint trajectory together. Treat the twenty simulator users as a small descriptive panel. Full-catalog diagnostic effects and sampled-candidate HR@10 measure different behavior; their relationship requires measurement.

For calibration, preregister perturbations, effect directions, thresholds, checkpoint schedule, and correlation analysis before examining benchmark validation outcomes. Keep the benchmark’s 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and seed=42 fixed. Measure diagnostic–HR@10 associations across checkpoints, accounting for shared users and correlated checkpoints; association does not establish causation. Learn any thresholds from training-history-only internal calibration, preserving official splits, then freeze them before benchmark validation. Otherwise report exploratory associations without threshold claims. [Model-selection guidance](https://scikit-learn.org/0.23/auto_examples/model_selection/plot_nested_cross_validation_iris.html) explains why tuning and assessing thresholds on identical validation outcomes creates optimistic bias.
